title: Monthly billing
description:
A subscription started on some date is billed every month on the same day of the month, or on the last day when that month is shorter. Write `public static class Billing` with:

- `public static DateOnly BillingDate(DateOnly start, int n)`: the date of the `n`th bill (bill 0 is on `start`). For a start on the 31st, February's bill is on the 28th (or 29th), and March's is back on the 31st.
- `public static decimal Prorate(DateOnly from, DateOnly to, decimal monthlyPrice, DateOnly start)`: the price for the days from `from` (included) to `to` (excluded) inside one billing period, as `monthlyPrice * days / daysInPeriod`, rounded to 2 places with `MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero`. The period is the one starting on the last billing date at or before `from`; throw `ArgumentException` when `to` is before `from` or after the end of that period.
hints: Work out the month first (`new DateOnly(start.Year, start.Month, 1).AddMonths(n)`), then the day as `Math.Min(start.Day, DateTime.DaysInMonth(...))`: this is why the 31st comes back in March (lesson 8.04).
`DayNumber` differences count days exactly, with no time zones involved.
